customization.summary: Managed sandbox microVMs with custom images containing sandbox-api, memory-sized CPU, network/proxy options, volumes and previews. CPU is coupled to RAM. Current adapter requests a unique per-attempt name, py-app:latest, 4096 MB, us-pdx-1 and ttl=1h; options allow alternate image/memory/region/TTL. Exact requested settings and guest observations are recorded in tested-configurations.json. No GPU deployment tested.

features.notes: Dockerfile/custom registry images must include sandbox-api; SDK ImageInstance injects the binary/default entrypoint. Generic unmodified Docker Hub images cannot directly act as sandbox images. Default slimming removes build-time compilers/caches; opt out where runtime builds need them. Adapter requests a mutable prebuilt py-app:latest tag.

Official sandbox use cases describe autonomous package installation and process execution. Availability depends on image tools, writable RAM-backed filesystem and egress policy. Legacy package_ecosystem report establishes pip availability, not a verified package installation; no new evaluated installation report was available.

CPU follows selected memory, not an independent CPU field in inspected SandboxRuntime. API description says memory MB/2048 (4096 MB=2 CPUs), while overview examples say 8 GB=4 cores and 16 GB=6 cores. Do not extrapolate a universal linear mapping or assign physical/vCPU equivalence without inventory. Adapter requests 4096 MB; actual existing-instance CPU is unknown.

memory is documented in MB; limits depend on account tier, custom pricing advertises up to 256 GB. Image base is read-only EROFS with writable tmpfs layer sharing RAM, approximately 50% reserved when possible. memory=4096 is a requested creation value, not measured process-available RAM; create_if_not_exists does not reconfigure existing instances.

No GPU reservation field in the inspected sandbox API/runtime configuration or explicit managed Sandbox GPU offering verified. Agent Hosting, model integrations, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES image examples, NVIDIA-branded tools and custom hardware marketing do not prove sandbox GPU access. No GPU requested or tested. Absence of documentation is not an explicit unsupported contract.

Public-preview proxy domain/method/path filters; environment-variable routing alone can be bypassed. Explicit firewall rulesets=[proxy] at creation enforces proxy egress, documented for Mark 3.0 not Carbon/3.1. API relocates allow/deny fields under network.proxy and has conflicting rule-precedence wording versus guide; verify exact version semantics before relying on overlap. Adapter configures no network restriction.

Standby snapshots retain state; attached Volumes survive deletion. Current guide limits one volume per sandbox, same region, create-time attach. Adapter mounts no durable storage and deletes its owned sandbox during cleanup/teardown with errors propagated.

Named lookup/reuse and standby restore are documented. Adapter now uses a unique per-attempt sandbox and does not declare reusable session calls. Legacy single-script multi-turn is not separate-call or standby/resume evidence.

process.exec accepts arbitrary shell command strings; named process wait/kill supported. Adapter always runs an uploaded Python script and combines logs. Without keepAlive, documented timeout bounds waiting and does not auto-kill process; adapter reports timed_out on wait timeout but does not call process.kill.

Provider supports native binary read/write and multipart transfer (direct HTTP request cap 5 MB, SDK chunks larger writes). Current adapter instead UTF-8-decodes inputs with errors=ignore, text-writes, and text-reads only /tmp/transformed_output.txt. Legacy 6000-byte text roundtrip does not validate arbitrary binary or multi-file fidelity.

Creation-time API ports and dynamic public/private token previews; preview URLs can use custom domains. API reserves 80/443/8080; preview guide explicitly forbids port 80. Bind to injected HOST; active WebSocket connections have timeout/reconnect constraints. Adapter exposes no ports/previews.

Pricing describes bring-your-own-metal: customer bare metal in own VPC connected privately to Blaxel control plane, with quote/custom hardware. This is partial infrastructure control, not a verified wholly self-operated control plane/runtime distribution. Evaluated path remains managed cloud.

No provider-native customer KMS encryption-key binding/rotation/revocation contract for sandbox snapshots, volumes, images or logs verified in inspected sources. BYOM, encrypted secrets or ZDR assertions do not establish CMEK. Adapter declares cmek_supported=False without an encryption test.

pricing.model: Active Sandbox compute billed by allocated GB RAM-second with CPU included; separate snapshot/image/volume storage while retained; standby has no compute charge.

pricing.limitations: Official public rates retrieved 2026-10-13; GB labels are retained and not silently converted to GiB. Memory API uses MB; exact MB-to-billable-GB convention not established. Snapshot/image/volume charges can continue while idle. Quota top-ups are wallet prepayment, not flat plan fees; eligibility is rolling 30-day real-money top-ups, promo credits do not count. Up to $200 credits advertised, account entitlement unverified. Agent/MCP/Batch Jobs pricing is a different product and is excluded from Sandbox compute rate. Legacy report fixed rates/resources have no billing verification or dated rate provenance. No price-change conclusion supported.
